audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Volibear Levels 2 through First item; the packet chart gives Sett Levels 2-5 and calls first item and 2+ items skill fights. The whys were also written against a different set of stage boundaries than their own labels (whys[2] talked about level 6 while sitting in the Level 3 row).
audit.why: Facebreaker reaches 490 against Thundering Smash's 300, and Volibear's Q is 12s at rank 1 against Sett's 13s E — Sett starts the level 2-5 trades. Volibear's real spike is Stormbringer at 6.
audit.corrected: Volibear / Sett / Sett / Sett / Volibear / Skill / Skill, with each why rewritten to its own row.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was described as Sett's window and Stormbringer was never named.
audit.why: Stormbringer is a 550-range leap on 160/135/110s that grants bonus health and temporarily disables nearby enemy towers — it is the strongest dive tool in the lane and it is why level 6 is Volibear's.
audit.corrected: phases/whys row 4 and spikes[1] now name Stormbringer and state the tower disable and bonus health.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four fields claimed Volibear's R silences; one called Thundering Smash a knockup; one invented the ability name 'Pit Grit' for Sett's Grit.
audit.why: Riot's text for Stormbringer is a leap with a slow, bonus health and a tower disable — no silence anywhere in the kit. Thundering Smash stuns (hardCC), it does not knock up, and it carries the autoReset flag, so the tell is the attack wind-up rather than the cast. Frenzied Maul is a 5s cooldown on-hit heal.
audit.corrected: Silence claims removed, stun and auto-reset stated, 'Pit Grit' removed, and Grievous Wounds timing tied to Frenzied Maul.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flagged zero cooldown-sequencing cues and no named abilities.
audit.why: None of Volibear's real cooldowns appeared anywhere in the matchup.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries Q 12s, E flat 16s and W 5s with the sequencing each implies.

edits.before: - Volibear Thundering Smash (Stun): matchup-defining — His engage. Bait it before yours. Track it before every engage. - Volibear Thundering Smash: Move speed toward enemies; the next auto stuns after running them down. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Volibear Thundering Smash (Q): 12s at rank 1 — it is an auto reset, so the attack wind-up is your cue to step out, not the cast. - Sky Splitter (E): flat 16s, shields him only if he stands in his own blast. - Frenzied Maul (W): 5s — buy anti-heal.

edits.before: Volibear: His level 1-2 Q knockup and W bite out-trade Sett before Pit Grit builds any meaningful grit shield.
edits.after: Volibear: Thundering Smash (Q) stuns and Frenzied Maul (W) heals him before Sett has any Grit banked at all.

edits.before: Sett: With Q and W stacked at 3-5, Sett wins the sustained brawl and Facebreaker locks Voli in for full Haymaker punches.
edits.after: Sett: Level 2 Knuckle Down plus a Grit-fed Haymaker out-trades Volibear while Thundering Smash sits on its 12s cooldown.

edits.before: Sett: At 6 Sett's grab under tower flips Voli's own dive into a kill; grit-shielded trades still beat his sustain here.
edits.after: Sett: Facebreaker at 490 out-reaches Thundering Smash's 300, so Sett starts every level-3 trade and cashes the Grit shield.

edits.before: Sett: Through the first-item spike Sett's Haymaker true damage keeps punishing Voli inside the grit window before his passive scales.
edits.after: Sett: Levels 4-5 Haymaker's true-damage centre ignores Volibear's armour, and Frenzied Maul's heal cannot keep pace without anti-heal.

edits.before: Volibear: After items Voli's sustain and passive shields survive Sett's burst and even bear-form trades tilt back to him.
edits.after: Volibear: Stormbringer (R) leaps 550, disables your tower and gives him bonus health — his level 6 beats yours in a straight dive.

edits.before: Skill: Late grouped fights hinge on landing R first; Sett peels, Voli silences, and neither reliably wins the 1v1.
edits.after: Skill: Late fights hinge on landing R first; Sett suplexes a diver out, Volibear leaps in and disables the tower behind you.

edits.before: Both ults are point-blank commit tools. His R silences and empowers his sustain, so hold The Show Stopper to grab him mid-dash or answer his all-in. Grabbing him into your tower flips his engage into your kill.
edits.after: Stormbringer (R) is a 550-range leap that disables your tower and gives him bonus health — it is a dive tool, not a silence. Hold The Show Stopper to catch him as he lands and drag him back out of the dive.

edits.before: Teamfights favor whoever lands their engage first. Your R peels a diver off your carry; his R silence-locks yours. Roughly even -- side-lane 1v1 slightly his, grouped skirmishes slightly yours with a good grab.
edits.after: Teamfights favor whoever lands engage first. Your R peels a diver off your carry; his R lands him on top of it with bonus health and your tower switched off. Even — side-lane his, grouped yours with a grab.

edits.before: He edges the very early skirmish -- his Q knockup and W bite out-trade you before your grit builds. Play the first two levels for CS, soak minion damage into grit, and avoid extended trades until you have your kit online.
edits.after: He edges level 1 — Thundering Smash (Q) stuns on the follow-up auto, and Frenzied Maul (W) heals him on the second cast. Play it for CS, soak minion damage into Grit, and take no extended trade before level 2.

edits.before: It levels back out. His item-scaled sustain and passive shields let him survive your burst, and his R silence shuts down your engage. Fights come down to who lands their initiation first -- treat it as a coinflip skirmish.
edits.after: It levels back out. Frenzied Maul's heal and Sky Splitter's shield let him survive your burst, and Stormbringer's bonus health carries him through a full Haymaker. Fights come down to who commits first — treat it as a coinflip.

notes: The content whys were written against different stage boundaries than their labels (an off-by-one against the Level 1/2/3/4-5/6/1st item/2+ rows); each has been rewritten to its own row. Volibear's R does not silence — that claim appeared in four places and is removed. 'Pit Grit' was a fabricated name for Sett's Grit.
